items.feedback: Right: the loop of action, result and next step is the structure; a longer prompt or bigger model only changes what one call can do.

You assumed the model reaches into the booking system itself. It can't: it only outputs text, here a structured request naming check_calendar with the laser cutter and tomorrow's date. The program around it runs the tool and sends back the result.
Right: the context already holds all 40 steps, so what's missing is a stopping condition, and a step limit supplies one.

Same misconception as q2: the model doesn't run the tools. Each model call ends in one tool request or the final answer, and the program runs the tool between calls. Three tool requests plus the final answer is 4 calls.
"Sends it back to the model" is the what. The why is missing: the model needs the result in its next input to decide its next step or write the final answer.

The first half is right: the model picks from the names and descriptions it is sent. The second half is wrong: the model doesn't remember past choices across sessions. It starts each session blank, and any memory has to be built into the program and sent in as text.

summary: You have the loop's shape and tool descriptions down, but you credit the model with doing things only the program does: running tools and remembering. Work on separating what the model outputs (text) from what the program does (runs tools, stores and resends information). Redraw your laser cutter trace as two columns, model and program, marking each step.
